overview: Tawantinsuyu joined diverse Andean regions through roads, administration and local labor. Its infrastructure drew on earlier Andean traditions and adapted construction to mountains, valleys and coastal environments.

items.text: Road builders used bridges, stairs, paving and drainage suited to different terrain. The network linked centers of production, government and worship.
Communities built and maintained terraces that created level planting areas while resisting erosion. Water conduits also protected roads from damaging runoff.
Stone channels and storage facilities managed rainfall and snowmelt for resources shared among families.
Colcas were storehouses whose siting and construction kept supplies cool and dry. Their contents included potatoes, maize, quinoa, clothing and tools.
The road system moved goods including textiles, feathers, food and shell. It incorporated earlier routes and knowledge from Andean communities.
Andean languages and traditions continued under Spanish rule. Weavers combined established textile techniques and designs with new imagery.

fall.text: Pizarro captured Atahualpa in 1532 and had him killed in 1533. Spanish conquest dismantled imperial government, while Andean peoples continued and adapted their traditions.
